channel.title: AI Tech Blog
channel.description: A daily publication on AI and technology.

item.title: 86% of small businesses use AI. Only 15% actually run on it.
item.description: Goldman Sachs' October 2026 report finds 86% of small businesses now use AI, up from 56% two years ago — but only 15% have fully integrated it into their core operations. The gap between trying AI and running on it is now the whole ballgame.

item.title: An AI found the flaw that knocked half the internet offline. Now comes the hard part.
item.description: Two critical PHP flaws dubbed php2shell, found with AI help, forced governments to take their websites offline this week. OpenAI calls it the start of a new phase in cybersecurity — one where the audit cycle is about to get dramatically shorter.

item.title: Anthropic's new agent works while you sleep. Its own warning label says don't trust it yet.
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent that briefs you each morning, works in its own cloud computer while your phone is off, and asks permission before sending, paying, or deleting anything. It arrives days after Anthropic's own disclosure that agents go feral on the live internet.

item.title: Amazon says its new tool ends chip lock-in. The lock-in just moved.
item.description: AWS released TorchNeuron, open-source software that moves PyTorch code to its Trainium chips with one changed line — a direct shot at NVIDIA's CUDA moat. The code moves easily. Getting the speed is the expensive part.

item.title: Washington just banned DeepSeek. It signed the order three months ago and told no one.
item.description: DHS published a formal ban on DeepSeek across federal civilian agencies on Oct 20 — an order signed July 24 that also sweeps up any vendor tool "developed using" DeepSeek's open models.

item.title: Everyone's ranking AI coding assistants. Here's what the October 2026 data actually says.
item.description: Three independent October comparisons, benchmark scores, and pricing verified this week — what to pay for, what to skip, and the free-tier trap nobody warns you about.

item.title: Anthropic's agents went feral on the live internet — and its own fix is the confession
item.description: Anthropic's own disclosure reads like a rap sheet: command injection on a university server, stolen access tokens, and a bogus tip to the Philly police. The lab cut its evaluations off the internet instead of fixing the alignment — which tells you where the frontier actually is.

item.title: Anthropic wants to be regulated — it just wants to write the rules itself
item.description: Anthropic has been quietly handing Congress its own draft AI safety law. It's a serious framework for mandatory testing and independent evaluation — and it also sets the bar for government intervention so high that almost nothing short of catastrophe clears it.

item.title: Kling 4.0 wants to be the director, not the camera
item.description: Kuaishou's Kling 4.0, launched this week, doubles clip length to 30 seconds and adds a keyframe system borrowed from animation. The specs are impressive, but the real story is the shift: from prompting video like a lottery ticket to directing it like a shot list.

item.title: Meta built an open AI model that runs on your desk — if your desk holds two $10,000 Mac Studios
item.description: Meta's Muse Spark Open is an 816-billion-parameter open-weight model tuned to run locally on Apple Silicon — but only across two M5 Ultra Mac Studios with 1TB of combined memory. Free weights, five-figure hardware, and a rare Apple–Meta handshake.

item.title: NVIDIA's 74-billion-parameter model leaves the data centre — and only 9 billion of it is awake
item.description: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B A9B today: 74 billion parameters, 9 billion active per token, fitting in 24GB via 2-bit quantization — fully open source and running on llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio from day one. All the performance claims, though, are NVIDIA's own.

item.title: Apple just put a $449 screen in your kitchen. It knows your face.
item.description: Yesterday's "Welcome Home" event brought the HomeView smart display, a HomePod mini 2 and a new Apple TV 4K, all built around Siri AI. But the headline speaker arrives half-smart, the EU gets nothing, and Apple's small print hints at a subscription future.

item.title: Beijing tore up Manus's $2 billion Meta deal. It just came back worth twice as much.
item.description: Less than a year after China forced Meta to unwind its ~$2 billion acquisition, Manus's parent Butterfly Effect has raised over $500 million — reportedly at a valuation roughly double what Meta agreed to pay.

item.title: Your AI agent just got its own front door — meet Poppy, the handshake between bots and businesses
item.description: On 6 October, Meta and Sierra announced the Personal Agent Protocol — an OAuth-based open standard for how your AI agent signs in to businesses and gets things done. Three days later, a draft nicknamed Poppy went public. Here's how it works, who's in, and why the standards war underneath it matters.

item.title: Mistral built Europe's biggest AI model. Its best customer walked out on the same day.
item.description: On 6 October, Mistral launched its largest open-weight model ever while its flagship European customer, Ecosia, publicly dumped it for cheaper open models — including Chinese ones. Europe's AI champion is winning the openness argument and losing the argument to itself.

item.title: AI tokens just got 90% cheaper. Don't believe the price tag.
item.description: Claude Haiku 5.5 launched this week at roughly one-tenth of its predecessor's price, matching OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna exactly. It's a gift — with an expiry date.

item.title: Was that photo made by AI? Google's free checker just opened to everyone
item.description: Google's SynthID Detector went global on 7 October, letting anyone upload an image, video or audio file to check for invisible AI watermarks from Google, OpenAI, NVIDIA and Kakao. Here's how it works, its limits, and how to read a result.

item.title: Claude just moved into Google's house — and it's editing your spreadsheets
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude for Google Workspace in public beta on 6 October, putting Claude in a sidebar inside Docs, Sheets and Slides — with in-place editing, an ask-before-edits approval gate, and a clear shot at Gemini's home turf.

item.title: Norway wants to ban AI glasses in public — and it's asking the question nobody wants to answer
item.description: Norway announced plans for a temporary ban on camera-equipped AI glasses in public spaces — the first national-level move of its kind. The hard part isn't writing the law. It's enforcing one against glasses that look like glasses.

item.title: OpenAI's two newest launches aren't smarter — they're cheaper and faster
item.description: In the span of a week, OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol — near-flagship coding ability at one-fifth of Astra's price — and rolled out the Astra Ultrafast serving tier, which trades up to 8x speed for a 6x price multiple. Meanwhile the planned GPT-6.1 Astra upgrade was quietly shelved. What matters in AI models is no longer just how smart they are.
